items.title: cntrl
items.text:
Hardware-independent descriptions of MIDI controllers

The API Reference is generated from the Python source code.

items.title: Optional feature modules
items.text: Status: setup management and songs/setlists use the static module menu. Panic, the MIDI cable tester and MIDI Interface use the right-hand page cycle. Firmware-specific modules are registered by their target. The broader organization below remains guidance for subsequent features.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Organize features such as a MIDI monitor, MIDI cable tester and MIDI processor as small optional modules around a shared core. Each module should work without the others. Modules do not call one another directly.

items.title: Ownership and dependencies
items.text:
Each module owns its configuration, private state, pages, commands, button actions, processing logic and tests.

The core owns physical MIDI ports, input decoding, output scheduling, buttons, displays, storage and time. Modules access these through small interfaces rather than accessing hardware directly. Hardware-specific implementations stay in the existing maker directories.

firmware/include/cntrl/midi_outputs.h defines the enabled physical MIDI output connections in cntrl::midi::output_connections: currently DIN and TRS. Each connection carries its configuration name, display label and bridge route. USB outputs are listed separately. Routing, Panic, the cable tester and MIDI-interface output indicators use this shared metadata. Input ports remain independent. Omniports are not enabled by this extraction; their MIDI configuration, target driver support and presentation of additional ports remain later work.

Dependencies point from modules to shared core interfaces. The core coordinates modules through an explicit registry; it does not depend on individual modules' implementation details. Share functionality only when real modules need it.

items.title: MIDI roles
items.text:
Role Example Behavior Observer MIDI monitor Receives events without consuming or changing them Processor Filter, remapper, arpeggiator Receives events on an explicitly configured route and produces output Active tool MIDI cable tester Temporarily claims selected ports and runs a test

These roles describe participation, rather than requiring every module to implement the same set of methods.

Enabling a monitor must not change routing. A processor must not automatically receive everything another processor emits. A cable tester must not inject test messages into live performance routes.

items.title: Routing and resource ownership
items.text:
The core determines which events reach each module, where generated messages go, and whether ports are available. Processing chains are explicit routes, not implicit consequences of module registration order.

A monitor can observe configured points before or after processing. Observation does not consume an event or prevent its normal delivery.

An active tool explicitly claims the ports needed for its operation and releases them when finished or deactivated. The core coordinates access so test traffic does not interfere with performance traffic. Conflicting use must be resolved before the operation starts.

items.title: Installed and enabled
items.text:
Keep build inclusion separate from setup activation:

  • Installed: the firmware build includes the module. Excluded modules contribute no code or assets.
  • Enabled: the setup selects an installed module. Disabled modules perform no work.

Start with static linking and an explicit module registry. Runtime plugin loading, automatic discovery and a general dependency framework are unnecessary.

items.title: Lifecycle and execution
items.text:
A module exposes only the operations it needs: initialization, activation and deactivation, event handling, and advancement of scheduled work where applicable. Private state belongs to the module; shared hardware state belongs to the core.

Execution is cooperative and bounded. A busy monitor or processor must not stall MIDI delivery or the UI. Scheduled processing uses core-provided time and output scheduling rather than blocking waits.

items.title: Establishing the interfaces
items.text:
The cable tester, MIDI interface and Panic use target adapters for physical services while owning their own behavior; the right-page renderer supplies their shared display style. A future MIDI monitor should reuse those services. Establish additional shared interfaces only when another module actually needs them.

Verify each module's logic independently. Also verify that observers leave routing unchanged, processors follow configured routes, active tools respect port ownership, and deactivation releases resources. Hardware behavior requires separate physical verification.

items.title: Additional work beyond the prompt
items.text: None. Current modules are documented in midi-cable-test.md, midi-interface.md and panic.md.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
Formatting uses TOML configuration, object-attached partial styles, page fields, tag membership and host-side compilation.

Authors choose colors and font names. Text always fits automatically. No CSS parser, selector language or additional dependency is required.

items.title: Styles
items.text:
Use the same optional style structure on shows, windows, pages, tags, programs, patches and shared parameters. Keep page-specific field overrides in pages.PAGE.line_styles.FIELD.

Property Meaning foreground_color Text color background_color Color behind the line font_name Exact installed bitmap font family horizontal_scale Positive width multiplier; overrides the font default icon Image-file reference; empty string suppresses an inherited icon

All five properties are optional. Omission leaves the lower-precedence value unchanged. Merge individual properties, not whole style objects. Apply centrally defined application defaults only where no source supplies a value.

Retain the existing color syntax and target font validation. A name such as CourierPrimeBold identifies a family; Bold is documentation within the name. There are no weight, italic, synthesis or font fallback controls. Horizontal scaling changes glyph widths and spacing before automatic fitting, without changing the vertical scale. StillTime defaults to 1.5; all other fonts default to 1.0. Explicit style values override these font defaults.

Use show-level style for authored appearance defaults. Font names belong in styles; there is no separate show-level font setting.

Illustrative configuration:

[style]
foreground_color = 'black'
background_color = 'white'
font_name = 'Arial'

[tags.sax.style]
foreground_color = '0xD08000'

[tags.whole-system.style]
font_name = 'CourierPrimeBold'

[pages.patch]
fields = ['patch_cycle.name', 'display_name']

[pages.patch.line_styles.'patch_cycle.name']
foreground_color = 'blue'

[windows.next]
page = 'patch'

[windows.next.style]
background_color = 'white'

These colors illustrate configuration, not a new default pedal theme. Existing program and patch definitions can continue to include their own style blocks.

items.title: Resolution order
items.text:
Resolve each property from lowest to highest precedence:

  1. Application defaults.
  2. Show style.
  3. Window style.
  4. Page style.
  5. Applicable tag styles, in the order described below.
  6. Program style, for patch-content fields.
  7. Patch style, for patch-content fields.
  8. Shared parameter style, for that parameter's field.
  9. Page-specific field style.

Only consult sources belonging to the displayed field. The tags field uses tag styles but not program or patch styles. Navigation headings such as patch_cycle.name use show, window, page and field styles. Global fields do not acquire the current patch's tags or appearance.

The same page resolves against each window's own data item. Background color follows the same partial-override rules as foreground color and font name. There is no separate transparency model or CSS inheritance behavior.

items.title: Tag membership and style precedence
items.text:
Programs and patches retain independently authored tag lists. Tag membership does not change MIDI behavior or navigation patch cycles.

Apply the program's tags in listed order, followed by the patch's own tags in listed order. Within these tag layers, a later explicit property wins. Registry declaration order has no effect. Tags have no integer priority.

For example, program tags ['sax', 'bright'] apply sax then bright. Patch tags ['whole-system'] apply afterward. A tag that only changes the font leaves the earlier foreground color intact. Explicit program and patch styles still take precedence over all tag styles, as listed above.

A tag repeated in the patch's own list applies again at that later position; otherwise deduplication would prevent the local ordering from taking effect. The displayed tag names remain unique, in their existing first-occurrence order. Distinguish that membership list from the ordered style application.

Preserve the explicit lists separately through download/recompile. Do not store a flattened inherited list as the patch's own tags. Tags do not require style declarations; an undeclared tag contributes no style properties.

items.title: Automatic text fitting and painting
items.text:
Each nonempty field independently chooses the largest available bitmap face that fits the drawable window width and its allocated vertical space. Preserve glyph proportions. Short labels remain bounded by height so they cannot overlap other lines; unused horizontal space is acceptable.

There are no authored font_size or autoscale_fonts controls. Selected raster sizes and metrics are compiler details. The patch-manager card divides the window into three equal vertical bands. Its first band is reversed, using the heading color as background and the page background as text color. The second and third lines share the smaller fitting size, while retaining their font families. Other pages, including switch pages, retain their own layout rules.

Window padding, horizontal centering, field order and missing-value omission remain part of the page model. Transitions end with the destination appearance.

Already-sent text keeps its resolved foreground and uses alternating transparent pixels to expose the line background. Stippling remains application behavior; there is no extra style color or half setting.

items.title: Optional style icons
items.text:
Every style may include an optional icon image-file reference, for example icon = 'images/sax.png'. It follows the same property override order as colors and font names. Omission inherits; icon = '' explicitly suppresses an inherited icon. Programs, patches and tags have no separate direct icon property. Preserve partial styles, including empty icon strings, through download/recompile.

Image loading, path resolution, conversion, embedding, layout and rendering remain future work. Resolving the reference does not display an icon yet.

items.title: Pages and fields
items.text: Pages contain ordered field names, for example fields = ['patch_cycle.name', 'names.vl70m', 'names.patchman']. Each window supplies its own data item to the page. Missing and empty values are omitted; zero and false remain visible. Built-ins and shared parameters use one unique namespace. Unknown or duplicate field names are errors. Pages are bounded by record capacity and target height. See the application guide for the complete field catalogue and compiled format, and Patch authoring for styles generated automatically for cycles.

items.title: MIDI cable test
items.text:
The cable tester is the right-hand page after Firmware and before Panic. Opening it starts Off with both result rows empty. C toggles On/Off. F stops any active test and continues the page cycle. Re-entering never restores On.

The page uses the shared configurable background, white-on-black heading, and heavier text without wider spacing. DIN and TRS results occupy fixed middle rows; On/Off appears at the bottom above C. The other two displays remain in place.

While On, the module sends a stream of breath-controller messages on both test outputs. MIDI CC 2 is Breath Controller. DIN uses channel 1; TRS uses channel 2. Each output sends one message every 10 ms, with values cycling through 0..127. A late poll sends at most one message per output, without a catch-up burst. A blocked output does not block the other.

The two result lines correspond to the transmitting outputs:

Output Return input Result DIN DIN DIN on the first line DIN TRS DIN to TRS on the first line TRS TRS TRS on the second line TRS DIN TRS to DIN on the second line

Only complete CC 2 messages on the appropriate channel, with a recently sent value, count as returns. The receiver handles running status and interleaved real-time messages using the shared MIDI parser. Each output retains its last eight accepted test values. A result disappears after 250 ms without a matching return. Switching Off clears both results immediately.

This checks delivery of MIDI messages, not individual connector-pin continuity.

items.title: Boundaries
items.text:
firmware/include/cntrl/cable_test.h owns message generation, return matching and a display-independent status snapshot. It uses the shared MIDI sink and parser. The target owns port access and navigation; the shared right-page renderer supplies the layout.

Browsing the page while Off leaves normal MIDI operation unchanged. Starting a test requires pending performance sends and setup transfers to finish. While On, the normal USB MIDI bridge is suspended, USB input is discarded, and physical input goes to the tester without forwarding. Performance buttons are inactive; C stops testing and F leaves the page. Test messages go directly to bounded physical output buffers, so no test backlog survives stopping. Bytes already handed to the UART finish transmitting. Stopping restores the setup's bridge setting. Leaving performance mode also stops the test.

items.title: Verification
items.text: Portable native tests cover Off on entry, channel/controller/output selection, all four labels, expiry, unrelated messages, running status, failed sends, re-entry and timestamp wraparound. Firmware builds must succeed with the tester included and excluded. Physical loopback and display behavior require separate pedal verification.

items.title: USB MIDI interface page
items.text:
MIDI Interface follows Panic at the end of the right-hand page cycle. It opens with the setup's current bridge state and does not change routing on entry. C temporarily toggles forwarding; F continues cycling and restores the setup setting if it was changed. The setup itself is not edited or saved.

The page uses the shared background, heading and heavier text. It shows host connection, four activity indicators and On/Off above C. The other two displays stay in place, and brightness is unchanged. Host connected means the USB device has been configured by the computer, not that a DAW opened a MIDI port.

DIN in and TRS in indicate complete received MIDI packets, including real-time and streamed SysEx, independently of onward queue acceptance. DIN out and TRS out indicate successful physical transmitter submissions, rather than USB reception or queue insertion. A lit output does not establish cable continuity or receipt by an instrument. Each indicator remains lit for 100 ms after its latest event. Off, exit and disconnection clear activity; reconnection does not replay it.

On enables the existing physical-to-USB and USB-to-physical routes without USB re-enumeration. It generates no test messages and adds no physical MIDI thru or USB-host routing. With no computer connected it remains responsive, reports No host, and does not retain physical input for later replay. Off clears bridge queues and parser state, preserving accepted pedal work and required SysEx termination. Normal performance controls remain available on this page.

firmware/include/cntrl/midi_interface.h owns the switch, activity state and display-independent status snapshot. The shared right-page renderer supplies the layout. MidiInterfaceControl supplies temporary bridge control and restores the setup preference on exit. The target supplies host and activity events and optional build inclusion. There is no dependency on the cable-test module or second implementation of MIDI forwarding.

Native tests cover lifecycle, setting restoration, host state, independent activity, expiry and timer rollover, stale-state clearing and disconnected-input parsing. Target-specific qualification, deployment and remaining physical checks are recorded in the hardware investigation and target guide.

items.title: Switch assignments
items.text:
Switches is an optional module for press, momentary and latched Patch assignments. Open it from the module menu. Every visit starts locally Off without transmitting anything. Held entry switches must be released before they activate an assignment.

Configure assignments in the performance setup:

[switches.sustain]
button = 'A'
mode = 'momentary'
on = { type = 'control-change', output = 'din', channel = 1, controller = 64, value = 127 }
off = { type = 'control-change', output = 'din', channel = 1, controller = 64, value = 0 }

[switches.solo]
button = 'B'
mode = 'latched'
on = { type = 'control-change', output = 'trs', channel = 2, controller = 7, value = 110 }
off = { type = 'control-change', output = 'trs', channel = 2, controller = 7, value = 85 }

[switches.start]
button = 'C'
on = { type = 'midi', output = 'din', bytes = [0xFA] }

press is the default mode and requires only on; it forbids off. Each new press invokes the Patch once. A momentary switch requests On when pressed and Off when released. A latched switch alternates states on successive presses. Both persistent modes require an explicit off Patch. On and Off may have different Patch types, outputs and channels.

Each branch accepts the common Patch representation, including inline program selections, sequences and stable references such as { type = 'reference', patch = 'clean' }. Program selections use instrument aliases; other MIDI variants name their output directly. Definitions are keyed by patches.clean, independently of their display labels.

Persistent assignments reserve the controls their reachable patches affect. Raw MIDI and SysEx reserve their entire destination output until Off cleanup or explicit abandonment. Other assignments cannot share those reserved resources. Two press assignments can share controls because each invocation completes its accepted work. Firmware visits and operations that leave this context are allowed only in press assignments. Other assignments finish cleanup before the context is left.

An optional assignment name defaults to its dictionary key; style uses the normal formatting properties. The optional pages.switches page accepts up to three switch, parameter or global-setting fields. Its default fields are switch.name, switch.mode and switch.state. switch.name includes the button in its label; switch.button exposes just that button. Status text is fitted against all possible status strings at compile time. Icons remain references for future use.

The page displays On, Off, Pending, Completed locally, Unknown remote state or Failed / unknown. These describe local execution and scheduling; completion does not acknowledge receipt by an instrument. Off executes its authored Patch and does not reconstruct the previous sound or roll back effects.

F begins cleanup and waits for accepted On/Off work to finish. F again abandons blocked cleanup. Disconnecting an active output marks its state unknown. Reconnecting never replays old work; an explicit new activation establishes the Off baseline before On. Configuration and asset replacement stay locked while the module or an invocation holds its source data. Status queries remain available. Program-selection Undo is separate from switch state.

Each assignment uses the shared Patch executor and its reserved scheduler owner. Backpressure preserves accepted work and required Off cleanup. Referenced source documents remain pinned for the assignment context, so pending work cannot read replaced configuration or staging bytes. Storage and memory limits are actual resource limits; there is no separate short-message command buffer or fixed sequence-depth restriction.

Live On/Off state is never persisted. This configuration uses the current compiled setup format and the tagged authoring schema. Older setups need conversion and recompilation; there is no legacy firmware decoder. See Patch authoring for the complete schema and required authoring changes. Exports after pedal program edits canonicalize synthesizer-name metadata while preserving MIDI selections and the visible labels; recompiling that canonical export is stable.

Native sanitizer tests cover edge handling, latching, queue pressure, cleanup, abandonment, disconnect/rearm and malformed records. Python tests cover schema errors, composed ownership, target capacity and exact export/recompile equality. Physical latency, switches and external MIDI reception require qualification on the pedal.

items.title: Panic page
items.text:
Panic follows MIDI Cable Test in the right-hand page cycle. It uses the shared background, heading and text style, with press/hold instructions and a Ready/Sending indicator. The other two displays stay in place.

Press C to start and temporarily set the screens to maximum brightness. Release C to restore the brightness that was active on entry. Browsing the page sends nothing and leaves normal MIDI routing unchanged.

A press starts this sequence on every available MIDI output, on channels 1..16:

  1. All Notes Off: CC 123, value 0.
  2. All Sound Off: CC 120, value 0.
  3. Reset All Controllers: CC 121, value 0.

A tap completes this first controller sweep even after C is released. Once all outputs have completed it, a continued hold starts Note Off messages with velocity 0, covering every note on every channel and output. Notes described to the user as 1..128 are encoded as MIDI values 0..127.

If C remains held after the Note Off sweep, repeat from the controller messages. Release during Note Off or a subsequent controller sweep to stop scheduling further messages. F cancels even the first sweep, restores brightness if needed, and continues the page cycle. Re-entry is idle.

items.title: Implementation boundaries
items.text:
firmware/include/cntrl/panic.h owns the bounded state machine and brightness feedback. The shared right-page renderer supplies its display. PanicOutputs provides output availability and nonblocking three-byte transmission. The module has no dependency on the cable tester or MIDI interface module.

Progress is independent per output, with a barrier between controller and Note Off sweeps. A blocked output is retried without duplicating or skipping messages and cannot starve another output. An unavailable output is skipped for that sweep. Each poll attempts at most one message; no busy waits or large generated message buffers are used.

The target pauses ordinary bridging while Panic owns the ports, then restores the setup's bridge setting when sending finishes or the page is left. Messages go directly to bounded transmitter buffers rather than building up a software backlog after release. Bytes already accepted by a transmitter finish transmitting.

items.title: Verification
items.text: Native tests cover the shared page layout, full controller and Note Off sequences on all outputs/channels, repetition, tap/hold/release, brightness restoration, retry, disconnection, cancellation and re-entry. Physical message capture and visible hold feedback require pedal verification.

items.title: Patches, switches and songs
items.text:
patch_cycles maps names to ordered lists of patches. A tag classifies a program or patch independently of those lists. Items use a tags list; the setup's optional [tags.NAME.style] tables define styles for selected tags. Tags do not need a declaration to be used.

A fully specified Patch is an executable table with a required type. The same table works in a named definition, a browser patch cycle, a switch assignment, a song position or a sequence. A sequence executes all its children on one activation. A song advances one position at a time.

items.title: Patch window presentation
items.text:
The patch-manager window is divided into three equal vertical bands. The top band is reversed across its full width. Its background uses the heading's resolved patch color and its text uses the page background. The second and third displayed lines use the smaller of their fitted sizes, retaining their font families. If the families have different bitmap sizes, the largest shared size at or below that limit is used. Switch pages retain their independent line sizing.

Styles may set horizontal_scale to a positive width multiplier. It participates in the usual style cascade and overrides the selected font's default. StillTime defaults to 1.5; other fonts default to 1.0. Fitting includes the scaled width.

items.title: Automatic cycle styles
items.text:
Setup-level fill_in_styles = true (the default) fills missing formatting for each cycle and its program lines. Explicit show, window, page, tag, program, patch and field styles still override these generated defaults per property. Global parameter and switch fields keep their existing formatting.

seed = 0
fill_in_styles = true
background_color = '0xFFF8D8'

Every cycle uses the same pale yellow background by default. Each cycle also gets a random available font, shared with its programs. All available font families are used before repeating, with adjacent repeats avoided when possible. Available families include target fonts and configured [fonts] entries.

For N cycles, foreground generation starts with the configured background color as an anchor. It greedily chooses N other colors, maximizing each new color's minimum squared RGB distance from the anchor and earlier choices. Candidates are a bounded RGB grid with channel values 0, 32, 64, 96, 128, 160, 192, 224 and 255, restricted to weighted RGB brightness below 50%: (0.299 R + 0.587 G + 0.114 B) / 255 < 0.5. This is an approximate perceived-brightness measure, not linear-light luminance. Explicitly authored foreground colors are unchanged. This is a farthest-point heuristic, not a guarantee of the global optimum. The N foregrounds are distinct; the background anchor is not assigned to a cycle. Existing contrast warnings remain.

One local random generator controls all these choices. Integer seed defaults to 0, making repeated compilation deterministic. Python callers may pass seed=None for a fresh one-time seed; TOML has no null literal. The compiled setup records that chosen seed, so downloading and recompiling preserves the appearance. Set fill_in_styles = false to retain only authored styling and application defaults. Styles are generated during compilation, with no pedal random generator or new firmware record format.

items.title: Simple program lists
items.text:
For an instrument that stays in one bank, list its program names in order:

[instruments.synth]
channel = 1
output = 'din'
programs = ['Piano', 'Flute', {}, 'Strings']

[patch_cycles]
Live = ['Piano', 'Flute', 'Strings']

Array positions are program numbers 1 through 128. An empty table {} leaves that position unnamed without moving subsequent programs. A flat array sends Program Change only: it does not select bank 0 or send either bank-select controller. Select the desired bank on the instrument before using the setup.

An entry can also be a metadata table, for example {name = 'Flute', tags = 'woodwind,solo'}. Tags accept a list of strings or a string separated by commas or colons. Program numbers and instrument identities come from the containing structure and cannot be repeated inside these entries.

In a patch cycle, a string looks up an exact program name. If a name occurs more than once, qualify it with {name = 'Flute', instrument = 'synth', bank = 3}, using whichever qualifiers are needed to select one program. These shorthand entries can include presentation properties, volume and pan. Named patches, switch assignments, sequences and songs continue to use explicit typed Patches.

For explicit banks, use a table whose keys are bank numbers:

[instruments.synth]
channel = 1
output = 'din'

[instruments.synth.programs]
0 = ['Piano', 'Flute']
3 = ['Lead', 'Strings']

[[definitions.setups]]
instrument = 'synth'
name = 'default'

[definitions.setups.banks.0]
lsb = 0

[definitions.setups.banks.3]
lsb = 3

[patch_cycles]
Live = ['Piano', 'Lead']

Explicit banks need mappings in the setup definition. msb is the value sent on CC 0; lsb is the value sent on CC 32. Only the configured controllers are sent. The example configures CC 32 alone. The compiler does not guess a device's bank mapping from its name or a catalogue's bank numbers.

The instrument identity defaults to its table key, and setup defaults to 'default'. A setup with no bank mappings or initialization data needs no definition. Routing still requires channel and output. Catalogues containing only names and metadata can be supplied as --table files; routing then belongs in the show file.

When files are combined with +, different bank keys merge without changing program numbers. Equal program arrays are retained once; conflicting arrays are errors even with conflict avoidance enabled. Flat and bank-keyed catalogues for the same instrument cannot be mixed. Existing explicit configurations and examples remain supported. See examples/patch-switcher/program-changes.toml for a complete flat-list example.

The documented VL70-m and Patchman catalogues keep their fixed program information in instruments/vl70m.toml and instruments/patchman.toml. Personal classifications are in instruments/tags.toml. Load the relevant catalogue and the tags file as separate --table arguments, or combine them with +. The tags file groups exact program names under each instrument:

[instruments.patchman.tags]
trumpet = ['Trumpet', 'Maynard', 'Alpert']
sax = ['Alto Sax', 'TenorSax', 'Bari Sax']

Each tag applies to every matching program name in that instrument's loaded catalogue. Missing names in a loaded catalogue are errors. Instruments whose catalogues are not loaded are ignored, so one tags file can serve several shows. Tag-table order determines tag order when a program belongs to multiple tags. If a nondefault setup is needed, declare setup once in the instrument table. Changing a classification does not require editing the documented catalogue.

items.title: Several catalogues on one MIDI destination
items.text:
When two instruments receive the same Program Change, describe the route once and attach their aligned sound catalogues:

[instruments.both]
output = 'din'
channel = 1
catalogues = ['vl70-internal.toml', 'patchman-internal.toml']

[pages.patch]
fields = ['patch_cycle.name', 'names.vl70m', 'names.patchman']

[patch_cycles]
Live = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

Paths are relative to the file containing the declaration. Each catalogue must describe one distinct instrument and one nonempty bank, with the same number of named program slots as the other catalogues. Slots align by program number. The catalogue bank describes the sounds; it does not request bank-selection messages. Set the hardware to the desired bank before using this configuration.

Each activation sends one Program Change to the configured destination, regardless of the number of attached catalogues. Numeric cycle entries require exactly one configured destination; with several destinations, use explicit typed patches. Do not also supply programs on a declaration that uses catalogues.

The names.INSTRUMENT fields expose the documented sound names independently. They use the same fitting, spacing, styling and already-sent stippling as the ordinary patch name. display_name remains available and defaults to the two names joined with /, omitting identical duplicates. Exports retain both names inside the program metadata and are self-contained; they do not need the original catalogue files to recompile.

Loading --table instruments/tags.toml applies each underlying sound's tags to the shared program. The effective tags are their union, plus any tags on the patch. Unselected sounds in those source instruments are ignored when only the shared catalogue is loaded. This allows differently tagged sounds to share one action without changing the classifications of either sound.

examples/patch-switcher/dual-internal.toml represents all 64 paired Internal slots for the stock VL70-m and Patchman units on channel 1.

items.title: Explicit patches
items.text:
[instruments.piano]
output = 'din'
channel = 1

[[definitions.setups]]
instrument = 'piano'
name = 'default'

[patches.clean]
type = 'program-change'
instrument = 'piano'
program = 1
display_name = 'Clean piano'

[patches.intro]
type = 'sequence'
patches = [
    {type = 'state', operation = 'brightness', value = 192},
    {type = 'reference', patch = 'clean'},
    {type = 'control-change', output = 'trs', channel = 2, controller = 11, value = 100},
]

[patch_cycles]
Live = [{type = 'reference', patch = 'intro'}]

[switches.intro]
button = 'A'
on = {type = 'reference', patch = 'intro'}

Instrument declarations and their bank mappings retain their existing meaning. Switch-only setups can omit instruments, definitions, named patches and patch cycles when their patches do not use them. Named definitions have stable keys; their dictionary order does not define the browser order. patch_cycles supplies that order.

items.title: Patch types
items.text:
Type Required fields Optional executable fields program-change instrument, program bank, volume, pan control-change output, channel, controller, value None pitch-bend output, channel, value None nrpn output, channel, parameter, value None sysex output, data None midi output, bytes None state operation and the fields below None stock-firmware exit_buttons, such as 'A+F' None sequence patches, a list of Patch tables None reference patch, a stable definition key document

Every type can have name, display_name, style and tags presentation metadata. Named definitions default their label to their key. Inline patches use a description of the operation. References inherit the target's presentation; metadata on the reference occurrence overrides it. Children of a sequence do not replace the parent performance display.

Channels are 1..16. Programs use 1..128 or the existing program-name regular expression lookup. Volume, CC controllers and CC values use 0..127; pan uses -64..63. Pitch bend uses -8192..8191, with zero centered. NRPN parameters and values use 0..16383. Program selections send bank MSB, bank LSB, program, optional volume and optional pan, in that order. NRPN sends CC 99, 98, 6 and 38 as one ordered message sequence on its output, allowing MIDI real-time traffic to interleave.

SysEx data contains 0..127 payload bytes, without F0/F7; the compiler adds those delimiters. midi.bytes contains exactly one complete message including its status and any delimiters. Running status from another patch is never inherited. Long SysEx streams through the normal cooperative output scheduler. The target must support the named output; this format adds no output drivers.

items.title: State operations
items.text:

Brightness and USB interface state are runtime settings. Executing these patches does not write the setup. Persistent setup settings still use the existing explicit setup editing and Save workflow. There is no arbitrary attribute, expression or dictionary of arguments to evaluate.

items.title: Switch timing and ownership
items.text:
Switches use A through E; F remains the context's Back control. mode defaults to press, which requires on and forbids off. momentary requires both and requests On at press, Off at release. latched requires both and alternates on successive presses. On and Off may use different Patch types, outputs and channels.

The full reachable graph determines ownership, including both branches and referenced sequences. Readable MIDI reserves its known controls. Raw MIDI and SysEx in a persistent assignment reserve their entire output through Off cleanup or explicit abandonment. Other assignments cannot share that output. There is no automatic note ownership or inferred inverse. Accepted work completes before the required Off patch runs. A held entry switch must be released before it rearms.

Stock visits and context-leaving operations are allowed in press assignments and song positions. Either branch of a momentary or latched assignment must stay in its context. Other active assignments finish their explicit cleanup before a press assignment leaves. See switch controls.

items.title: References and song libraries
items.text:
[patches.borrowed]
type = 'reference'
document = 'other-setup'
patch = 'clean'

External references use the setup's logical name and a named patch's stable key. Display labels and instrument/program matching are not identities. The setup CLI loads adjacent other-setup.toml companions recursively and compiles the complete dependency graph before opening the transport. On the pedal, sources are checked and pinned before execution. Missing references and cycles fail before effects; pending work prevents replacement of its source data.

Song libraries have optional instruments, definitions, patches, fonts and tags context using the same authoring models. Each song's patches list contains ordinary Patch tables, with an optional id for the position's persistent occurrence identity. A nonempty library is compiled with --target; companion setups and font assets follow the existing copy/download workflow. Inline captures retain their compiled source; live references retain their stable document/key.

items.title: Completion, failure and stock return
items.text:
Execution is ordered across outputs. Backpressure leaves the current child pending. A failed child stops the invocation; completed effects are not rolled back. Completed locally means delivery to the local MIDI output, without an instrument acknowledgement. Disconnects or abandoned cleanup can leave remote state unknown. Undo restores known program selections and does not implicitly replay a composite or reverse state, SysEx or firmware visits.

A stock visit checkpoints the enclosing root, completed child ordinal, source fingerprint, caller and song/setlist occurrences when present. It also preserves the browser context and active brightness/interface settings needed to resume. Only an explicit stock return can resume. Its durable token is consumed before dispatch; changed sources, invalid records and ordinary boot never replay it. Remaining children finish before a song advances once to its next position. Power loss after consumption can leave an operation unexecuted or its result unknown, rather than risk sending it twice.

items.title: Required authoring and format changes
items.text:
The current setup format is 25; song records use CSG4. Setup window graphics and page references use physical left-to-right order: next (0), sent (1), undo (2). Recompile and upload matching setup and song documents together before using this firmware. Existing binary documents are rejected; no migration or dual execution path is provided. Keep backups before replacing existing device data. Exports after on-pedal program or bank edits preserve the current MIDI values and displayed labels while canonicalizing their source metadata. Further export/recompile cycles are stable.

  • Move the old browser-list dictionary from patches to patch_cycles. patches now holds reusable named Patch tables.
  • Rename groups to patch_cycles, group.name to patch_cycle.name, and categories membership and style definitions to tags. Program catalogues use the same tags membership field as patches.
  • Add type to every executable table. Replace delimiter shorthand with explicit program fields; strings are not references and bare lists are not sequences.
  • Replace function = 'stock-firmware' with type = 'stock-firmware'.
  • Replace actions with switches, and each old command with its complete Patch table. References use stable keys rather than display names. Use pages.switches and switch.* display fields for switch presentation.
  • Replace song instrument/program references with type = 'reference', document and patch. Inline program selections use the song library's instrument context.

Automated tests and target builds qualify encoding, scheduling, source lifetimes and continuation logic. Physical MIDI reception, switch timing and stock-return behavior for this format still require separate hardware qualification.

items.title: Setup revision history
items.text:
Every replacement of a valid saved setup first archives its outgoing bytes. Uploads, saved pedal edits and restores use the same path. Identical replacement bytes do not add an automatic revision. Named snapshots may deliberately copy an unchanged setup. History has no automatic pruning or small retention cap.

History is separate from the two current-save slots. A failed history write prevents replacement; an interrupted later save still has the two-slot recovery protection. Incomplete records are skipped. Revision numbers are never reused, including after deletion: empty history directories reserve those numbers.

items.title: Host commands
items.text:
Use cntrl setup history NAME ACTION --port PORT, with these actions:

  • list: list revisions newest first, with optional label, epoch timestamp and size.
  • save --label 'Friday rehearsal': snapshot the saved current setup.
  • download --revision N --output revision.bin: download exact compiled bytes, including versions unsupported by the running decoder. Existing files are not overwritten.
  • compare --revision N: show configuration paths and old/new values against Current.
  • restore --revision N: validate and restore through the regular save path.
  • delete --revision N --yes: explicitly delete one revision.
  • clear --yes: explicitly delete the setup's entire history.

Labels use the existing 63-character printable setup-name rules. The host sets the device clock before named snapshots. If the device has no reliable clock, timestamps are zero; revision numbers still determine order.

Comparison uses editable exports, preserving list order and excluding generated font sizes, placement records and checksums. The pedal provides a compact summary of changed patch records, routes, settings and authored metadata instead of a full textual diff. Raw authored metadata comparison can report a change when only its serialization differs; the host comparison resolves actual values.

items.title: Pedal
items.text:
Choose a setup, then History. Current offers C to save an unnamed snapshot; use the host for names. B browses older revisions, A returns to Current. Selecting a revision opens comparison; A/B browse the summary and Restore action. C on Restore commits it, while F returns without changing anything. Browsing and restoring send no MIDI. Revision number, timestamp and label identify each entry.

Restoring keeps the selected historical record unchanged and archives the outgoing Current, so another restore can reverse the operation. Normal setup deletion retains history; access it by setup name from the host. Recreating that name continues the same history.

items.title: Assets and limits
items.text:
A revision copies the setup document and its authored metadata, not external assets. Existing immutable font assets remain in storage. Restore validates the document and stages required fonts before replacing Current; missing assets or unsupported compiled versions fail without replacement. Unsupported revisions remain downloadable for recompilation with appropriate host tooling.

History work runs as cooperative jobs. Each main-loop step handles one directory entry or at most 512 bytes of file I/O. Snapshot hashing, writing and read-back verification yield between blocks, including the outgoing current-document read. Clear history traverses the directory once, deleting one record per step. The pedal displays Working while a history action is pending, then shows its result or error. Host operations receive progress replies during long jobs.

No history index is held in RAM and boot does not enumerate history. The state machine bounds application work; an individual SD library call can still have hardware-dependent latency. Storage calls, font loading and the existing final current-setup activation path are not hard real-time guarantees. Physical timing qualification is still required.

Native tests cover reversible restores, failed writes, deletion, interrupted records, more than 1,000 revisions, and per-step I/O limits with a 64 KiB document and more than 2,000 directory entries. Python tests compare configurations and exercise the real C++ command receiver through a pseudo-terminal, including progress replies. The cooperative implementation has been flashed and subsequent boots have loaded saved setups successfully. Dedicated physical history-workflow and storage timing qualification remain pending.

items.title: Firmware upload helper
items.text:
Use the running, user-launched upload helper for firmware flashing. Reuse that process; do not start a second server. It accepts an upload request for a fixed build image with an exact SHA-256, validates and snapshots the image, then calls the installed updater. It does not expose arbitrary commands or image paths.

Build and inspect the image first, close serial captures, request bootloader entry, verify device identity, then upload with the digest. Let the upload finish. Investigate write failures before retrying, and verify application status and saved setup data after USB returns. Firmware flashing and setup transfers are separate operations; the helper does not grant serial-transfer permissions.

The target-specific helper guide contains the implementation link, exact commands, device identity, image path, validation rules, startup and recovery instructions.

def load_catalogue(path: Traversable) -> dict[str, models.Controller]:
    """Load a catalogue file, excluding its shared ``@`` definitions."""
    data = tomlkit.loads(path.read_text()).unwrap()
    definitions = {k: v for k, v in data.items() if k.startswith('@')}
    return {
        k: models.Controller(
            name=v['name'],
            controls=[models.Button(id=c.lower(), name=c) for c in v['buttons']],
            displays=[_display(i, d) for i, d in enumerate(v['displays'], 1)],
            ports=[
                _port(f'{k}-{i}' if isinstance(v, list) else k, p, definitions)
                for k, v in v['ports'].items()
                for i, p in enumerate(v if isinstance(v, list) else [v], 1)
            ],
        )
        for k, v in data.items()
        if not k.startswith('@')
    }

class BitmapRaster:
    def __init__(self, path: Path, name: str, horizontal_scale: float) -> None:
        self.tables = native_tables(path.read_text(), name)
        self.horizontal_scale = horizontal_scale
        self.glyphs: dict[tuple[int, int], Glyph] = {}
        self.advances: dict[tuple[int, int], float] = {}

    def glyph(self, size: int, identifier: int) -> Glyph:
        key = size, identifier
        if key in self.glyphs:
            return self.glyphs[key]
        index, data, numbers = self.tables[size]
        _, _, first, last, _, _, bi, bw, bh, bx, by, bd, _, cap = numbers
        if not first <= identifier <= last:
            raise ValueError(f'bitmap font has no U+{identifier:04X}')
        offset = read_bits(index, (identifier - first) * bi, bi) * 8
        if read_bits(data, offset, 3):
            raise ValueError('unsupported bitmap glyph encoding')
        offset += 3
        values = []
        for bits, signed in [
            (bw, False),
            (bh, False),
            (bx, True),
            (by, True),
            (bd, False),
        ]:
            values.append(read_bits(data, offset, bits, signed))
            offset += bits
        width, height, left, bottom, advance = values
        rows: list[list[int]] = []
        while len(rows) < height:
            repeated = read_bits(data, offset, 1)
            offset += 1
            count = read_bits(data, offset, 3) + 2 if repeated else 1
            offset += 3 if repeated else 0
            row = [read_bits(data, offset + x, 1) for x in range(width)]
            offset += width
            rows.extend([row] * count)
        scaled_width = max(1, round(width * self.horizontal_scale)) if width else 0
        stride = (scaled_width + 7) // 8
        pixels = bytearray(stride * height)
        for y in range(height):
            for x in range(scaled_width):
                if rows[y][min(width - 1, int(x / self.horizontal_scale))]:
                    pixels[y * stride + x // 8] |= 128 >> (x % 8)
        self.advances[key] = advance * self.horizontal_scale
        self.glyphs[key] = Glyph(
            identifier=identifier,
            width=scaled_width,
            height=height,
            left=round(left * self.horizontal_scale),
            top=height + bottom - cap,
            pixels=bytes(pixels),
        )
        return self.glyphs[key]

    def shape(self, size: int, text: str) -> Run:
        positions = []
        cursor = 0.0
        left = right = top = bottom = 0
        for char in text:
            identifier = ord(char)
            glyph = self.glyph(size, identifier)
            x = round(cursor)
            positions.append([identifier, x, 0])
            left = min(left, x + glyph.left)
            right = max(right, x + glyph.left + glyph.width)
            top = min(top, -glyph.top)
            bottom = max(bottom, glyph.height - glyph.top)
            cursor += self.advances[size, identifier]
        return Run(
            positions=positions,
            left=left,
            width=max(right, round(cursor)) - left,
            top=top,
            bottom=bottom,
        )

def combine(
    stock: FirmwareImage, custom: FirmwareImage, hook: bytes, reader: int
) -> bytes:
    if stock.sha256 != STOCK_SHA256:
        raise ValueError('stock firmware does not match the traced v3.14.0 image')
    if (
        custom.origin != 0x60100000
        or custom.origin + len(custom.data) > 0x607C0000
        or len(custom.regions) != 1
        or len(custom.data) % 1024
        or not 0 < len(hook) <= 4096
        or not reader & 1
        or not 0x60083000 <= reader - 1 < 0x60083000 + len(hook)
    ):
        raise ValueError('invalid relocated image or stock hook layout')
    result = bytearray(b'\xff' * (0x100000 + len(custom.data)))
    result[: len(stock.data)] = stock.data
    result[0x100000:] = custom.data
    patches = [
        (0x18E0, bytes.fromhex('704700bf'), bytes.fromhex('81f08ebb')),
        (0x7C424, struct.pack('<I', 0x2649), struct.pack('<I', reader)),
        (0x15F0, struct.pack('<I', 0x20013CA0), struct.pack('<I', 0x20013DA0)),
        (0x1990, struct.pack('<I', 0x20013CA0), struct.pack('<I', 0x20013DA0)),
        (0x1024, struct.pack('<I', 0x83000), struct.pack('<I', len(result))),
        (
            0x1018,
            struct.pack('<I', 0x60082400),
            struct.pack('<I', stock.origin + len(result) - 3072),
        ),
    ]
    for offset, expected, replacement in patches:
        if result[offset : offset + len(expected)] != expected:
            raise ValueError(f'unexpected stock patch bytes at {offset:#x}')
        result[offset : offset + len(expected)] = replacement
    result[0x83000 : 0x83000 + len(hook)] = hook
    # This sector belongs to boot selection, not either application's image.
    struct.pack_into('<2I', result, 0x84000, 0x434E4254, 0xBCB1BDAB)
    return bytes(result)

def encode_hex(data: bytes) -> str:
    lines: list[str] = []
    upper = -1
    for offset in range(0, len(data), 16):
        address = 0x60000000 + offset
        if address >> 16 != upper:
            upper = address >> 16
            record = bytes([2, 0, 0, 4]) + upper.to_bytes(2, 'big')
            lines.append(':' + (record + bytes([-sum(record) & 255])).hex().upper())
        chunk = data[offset : offset + 16]
        record = bytes([len(chunk)]) + (address & 65535).to_bytes(2, 'big')
        record += b'\x00' + chunk
        lines.append(':' + (record + bytes([-sum(record) & 255])).hex().upper())
    lines.extend([':040000056000100087', ':00000001FF'])
    return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'

def build(command: Build) -> None:
    root = Path(__file__).parent / 'firmware'
    work = root / 'build/boot-switch'
    work.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    stock = read_hex(command.stock)
    if stock.sha256 != STOCK_SHA256:
        raise ValueError('stock firmware does not match the traced v3.14.0 image')
    core = root / '.tools/data/packages/teensy/hardware/avr/1.62.0'
    original = (core / 'cores/teensy4/imxrt1062_t41.ld').read_text()
    region = 'FLASH (rx): ORIGIN = 0x60000000, LENGTH = 7936K'
    if original.count(region) != 1:
        raise ValueError('unexpected Teensy linker script')
    linker = work / 'cntrl.ld'
    linker.write_text(
        original.replace(region, 'FLASH (rx): ORIGIN = 0x60100000, LENGTH = 6912K')
    )
    subprocess.run(
        [
            'make',
            '-C',
            str(root),
            'patch-switcher',
            f'PATCH_BUILD={work / "cntrl"}',
            f'PATCH_OUTPUT={work / "cntrl.hex"}',
            f'PATCH_LINKER={linker}',
        ],
        check=True,
    )
    custom = read_hex(work / 'cntrl.hex')
    entry = struct.unpack_from('<I', custom.data, 0x1004)[0]
    arm = root / '.tools/data/packages/teensy/tools/teensy-compile/15.2.1/arm/bin'
    tool = arm / 'arm-none-eabi'
    source = root / 'boot_switch'
    elf = work / 'hook.elf'
    subprocess.run(
        [
            f'{tool}-g++',
            '-mcpu=cortex-m7',
            '-mthumb',
            '-mfloat-abi=hard',
            '-mfpu=fpv5-d16',
            '-std=c++17',
            '-Os',
            '-ffreestanding',
            '-fno-exceptions',
            '-fno-rtti',
            '-fno-unwind-tables',
            '-fno-asynchronous-unwind-tables',
            '-nostdlib',
            '-Wall',
            '-Wextra',
            '-Werror',
            f'-DCNTRL_SWITCH_WINDOW_MS={round(command.switch_window * 1000)}',
            f'-Wl,-T,{source / "hook.ld"},--defsym,custom_entry={entry}',
            str(source / 'gate.S'),
            str(source / 'hook.cpp'),
            '-o',
            str(elf),
        ],
        check=True,
    )
    binary = work / 'hook.bin'
    subprocess.run(
        [f'{tool}-objcopy', '-O', 'binary', str(elf), str(binary)], check=True
    )
    symbols = subprocess.run(
        [f'{tool}-nm', '--defined-only', str(elf)],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    ).stdout
    addresses = {
        p[2]: int(p[0], 16) for s in symbols.splitlines() if len(p := s.split()) == 3
    }
    combined = combine(
        stock, custom, binary.read_bytes(), addresses['stock_reader'] | 1
    )
    output = work / 'combined.hex'
    output.write_text(encode_hex(combined))
    image = read_hex(output)
    validate_firmware(image)
    if image.data != combined:
        raise ValueError('combined HEX readback differs')
    print(
        f'{output}: patch mode by default; '
        f'stock exit pair is configured per visit, '
        f'{command.switch_window} seconds, no hold'
    )
    print(f'SHA256: {image.sha256}')

def read_bits(data: bytes, offset: int, count: int, signed: bool = False) -> int:
    value = 0
    for i in range(offset, offset + count):

def native_face(source: str, name: str, identifier: int) -> models.FontFace:
    sizes: dict[int, models.FontMetrics] = {}
    for size, (index, data, numbers) in native_tables(source, name).items():
        (
            version,
            reserved,
            first,
            last,
            second,
            second_last,
            bi,
            bw,
            bh,
            bx,
            by,
            bd,
            line,
            cap,
        ) = numbers
        if (version, reserved, first, last, second, second_last) != (
            1,
            0,
            32,
            126,
            0,
            0,
        ):
            raise ValueError(f'unsupported font encoding: {name}_{size}')
        glyphs = bytearray()
        top, bottom = 0, line
        for c in range(95):
            offset = read_bits(index, c * bi, bi) * 8
            if read_bits(data, offset, 3):
                raise ValueError('unsupported glyph encoding')
            offset += 3
            width = read_bits(data, offset, bw)
            offset += bw
            height = read_bits(data, offset, bh)
            offset += bh
            left = read_bits(data, offset, bx, True)
            offset += bx
            y = read_bits(data, offset, by, True)
            offset += by
            advance = read_bits(data, offset, bd)
            top = min(top, cap - height - y)
            bottom = max(bottom, cap - y)
            glyphs.extend([advance, left & 255, width])
        sizes[int(size)] = models.FontMetrics(
            line_height=bottom - top, top=-top, glyphs=glyphs.hex()
        )
    return models.FontFace(name=name, id=identifier, sizes=sizes)

def read_hex(path: Path) -> FirmwareImage:
    """Validate Intel HEX records and decode addresses, filling gaps with 0xff."""
    source = path.read_bytes()
    memory: dict[int, int] = {}
    records: Counter[int] = Counter()
    base = 0
    entry: int | None = None
    finished = False
    for number, line in enumerate(source.decode('ascii').splitlines(), 1):
        if finished or not line.startswith(':'):
            raise ValueError(f'line {number}: invalid record or data after EOF')
        record = bytes.fromhex(line[1:])
        if len(record) < 5 or len(record) != record[0] + 5:
            raise ValueError(f'line {number}: incorrect record length')
        if sum(record) % 256:
            raise ValueError(f'line {number}: invalid checksum')
        address = int.from_bytes(record[1:3], 'big')
        kind = record[3]
        payload = record[4:-1]
        records[kind] += 1
        if kind == 0:
            for index, byte in enumerate(payload):
                location = base + address + index
                if location in memory:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f'line {number}: overlapping data at {location:#x}'
                    )
                memory[location] = byte
        elif kind in (2, 4) and len(payload) == 2 and address == 0:
            base = int.from_bytes(payload, 'big') << (4 if kind == 2 else 16)
        elif kind == 5 and len(payload) == 4 and address == 0:
            entry = int.from_bytes(payload, 'big')
        elif kind == 1 and not payload and address == 0:
            finished = True
        else:
            raise ValueError(f'line {number}: unsupported or malformed record {kind}')
    if not finished or not memory:
        raise ValueError('image must contain data and an EOF record')

    addresses = sorted(memory)
    regions: list[AddressRange] = []
    start = previous = addresses[0]
    for address in addresses[1:]:
        if address != previous + 1:
            regions.append(AddressRange(start=start, end=previous + 1))
            start = address
        previous = address
    regions.append(AddressRange(start=start, end=previous + 1))
    origin = addresses[0]
    return FirmwareImage(
        origin=origin,
        entry=entry,
        data=bytes(memory.get(a, 0xFF) for a in range(origin, addresses[-1] + 1)),
        regions=regions,
        record_counts=dict(records),
        sha256=hashlib.sha256(source).hexdigest(),
    )

def inspect_firmware(path: Path, output_directory: Path) -> FirmwareImage:
    """Print i.MX RT image details and write derived analysis files.

    Output files are created exclusively so an existing artifact is not overwritten.
    The ELF is a flash-address wrapper for disassembly, not a flashable executable
    or a reconstruction of the runtime RAM mappings.
    """
    image = read_hex(path)
    if image.data[:4] != b'FCFB' or len(image.data) < 0x1060:
        raise ValueError('expected an i.MX RT FlexSPI flash image')
    ivt = struct.unpack_from('<8I', image.data, 0x1000)
    if ivt[0] != 0x432000D1:
        raise ValueError('unexpected i.MX RT image vector table')
    print('SHA256:', image.sha256)
    print('Record counts:', image.record_counts, '(all checksums valid)')
    print('HEX entry:', hex(image.entry) if image.entry is not None else None)
    print('Reset vector:', hex(ivt[1]))
    print('Regions:', [(hex(r.start), hex(r.end)) for r in image.regions])
    print('Populated bytes:', sum(r.end - r.start for r in image.regions))
    print('Image span:', len(image.data))
    print('Configured flash bytes:', struct.unpack_from('<I', image.data, 0x50)[0])
    for offset in (0x1000, 0x1020, 0x1040):
        print(
            f'Words at {image.origin + offset:#010x}:',
            [hex(w) for w in struct.unpack_from('<8I', image.data, offset)],
        )
    signature_offset = ivt[6] - image.origin
    if 0 <= signature_offset < len(image.data):
        signature = image.data[signature_offset:]
        print('CSF pointer:', hex(ivt[6]))
        print('Bytes from CSF to image end:', len(signature))
        print('CSF remainder all zero:', not any(signature))
    for offset in range(0, len(image.data), 65536):
        chunk = image.data[offset : offset + 65536]
        entropy = -sum(
            (n / len(chunk)) * math.log2(n / len(chunk))
            for n in Counter(chunk).values()
        )
        print(f'Entropy at {image.origin + offset:#010x}: {entropy:.3f}')

    strings = [
        (image.origin + m.start(), m.group().decode('ascii'))
        for m in re.finditer(rb'[\x20-\x7e]{6,}', image.data)
    ]
    print('ASCII strings of at least six characters:', len(strings))
    pattern = re.compile(
        r'teensy|arduino|morningstar|mc6|firmware|ILI9|ST77|GC9|SPI|i2c|uart|'
        r'relay|GPIO|sdFat|\.cpp|\.c\b|\.h\b|malloc|boot|usb|EEPROM|display|lcd|tft|imxrt',
        re.IGNORECASE,
    )
    for address, text in strings:
        if pattern.search(text):
            print(f'{address:#010x}: {text}')
        if 'test' in text.lower():
            locations: list[int] = []
            needle = struct.pack('<I', address)
            start = 0
            while (offset := image.data.find(needle, start)) >= 0:
                locations.append(image.origin + offset)
                start = offset + 1
            print(f'Raw flash pointers to {text!r}:', [hex(a) for a in locations])

    output_directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    artifacts = {
        'firmware.bin': image.data,
        'firmware.elf': _elf(image, ivt[1]),
        'strings.txt': ''.join(f'{a:#010x}: {s}\n' for a, s in strings).encode(),
    }
    for name, content in artifacts.items():
        with output_directory.joinpath(name).open('xb') as stream:
            stream.write(content)
    return image

def pack(
    outline: Outline | BitmapRaster,
    selected: dict[int, list[str]],
    metrics: dict[int, models.FontMetrics] | None = None,
) -> bytes:
    entries = []
    for size, texts in sorted(selected.items()):
        runs = {t: outline.shape(size, t) for t in sorted(set(texts))}
        identifiers = sorted({p[0] for r in runs.values() for p in r.positions})
        glyphs = [outline.glyph(size, i) for i in identifiers]
        index = bytearray()
        pixels = bytearray()
        for g in glyphs:
            index.extend(
                GLYPH.pack(g.identifier, g.width, g.height, g.left, g.top, len(pixels))
            )
            pixels.extend(g.pixels)
        # Numbers change on the pedal. Reserve their individual glyphs and
        # advances; all other text is drawn using its complete prepared run.
        characters = [t for t in runs if len(t) == 1 and t in NUMBERS]
        for c in characters:
            r = runs[c]
            if len(r.positions) != 1:
                raise ValueError(f'cannot use {c!r} as a runtime numeric glyph')
            index.extend(
                CHARACTER.pack(ord(c), identifiers.index(r.positions[0][0]), r.width)
            )
        for text, run in runs.items():
            encoded = text.encode('utf-8')
            index.extend(
                RUN.pack(len(encoded), run.left, run.width, len(run.positions))
            )
            index.extend(encoded)
            for identifier, x, y in run.positions:
                index.extend(POSITION.pack(identifiers.index(identifier), x, y))
        top = min((r.top for r in runs.values()), default=0)
        bottom = max(1, max((r.bottom for r in runs.values()), default=0))
        if isinstance(outline, Outline):
            bottom = max(bottom, outline.descent(size))
        height, baseline = (
            (metrics[size].line_height, metrics[size].top)
            if metrics
            else (max(1, bottom - top), -top)
        )
        fields = [
            size,
            2,
            0,
            0,
            0,

def entries(data: bytes) -> dict[int, tuple[list[int], bytes, bytes]]:
    if not 8 <= len(data) <= MAX_ASSET:
        raise ValueError('font asset exceeds 256 KiB or is truncated')
    magic, count = HEADER.unpack_from(data)
    if magic != b'CFN2' or not 1 <= count <= 32:
        raise ValueError('invalid font asset header')
    result = {}
    offset = HEADER.size
    for _ in range(count):
        if offset + ENTRY.size > len(data):
            raise ValueError('truncated font descriptor')
        fields = list(ENTRY.unpack_from(data, offset))
        size, ni, nd = fields[0], fields[-2], fields[-1]
        offset += ENTRY.size
        if (
            not size
            or size in result
            or fields[1:7] != [2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
            or not fields[13]
            or fields[14] > 128
            or ni + nd > 96 * 1024
            or offset + ni + nd > len(data)
        ):
            raise ValueError('invalid font descriptor')
        result[size] = (
            fields,
            data[offset : offset + ni],
            data[offset + ni : offset + ni + nd],
        )
        offset += ni + nd
    if offset != len(data):
        raise ValueError('trailing font asset data')
    return result

def main() -> None:
    options = tyro.cli(Options)
    if sys.platform != 'darwin':
        sys.exit('This qualification uses macOS CoreMIDI.')
    midi = Midi()
    try:
        sources, destinations = midi.endpoints(True), midi.endpoints(False)
        for n in sources:
            print(f'Input: {n}')
        for n in destinations:
            print(f'Output: {n}')
        if not options.run:
            return
        destination, source = destinations[options.destination], sources[options.source]
        midi.check(midi.core.MIDIPortConnectSource(midi.input, source, None))
        with SerialConnection(options.port, timeout=3) as connection:
            client = SetupClient(connection)
            before = client.request('CNTRL MIDI STATUS 0')
            print(before, flush=True)
            if before.split()[2] != str(int(options.expect_enabled)):
                raise ValueError(
                    'Bridge enabled state differs from requested qualification'
                )
            client.ok('CNTRL MIDI RESET')
            time.sleep(0.1)
            midi.data.clear()
            # Program changes and benign modulation controls, not note events.
            messages = b''.join(bytes((0xC0 | i % 16, i)) for i in range(128))
            messages += b''.join(bytes((0xB0 | i, 1, 0)) for i in range(16))
            midi.send(destination, messages)
            time.sleep(0.5)
            expected = messages if options.expect_enabled else b''
            if bytes(midi.data) != expected:
                raise ValueError(
                    f'Short-message mismatch: expected {len(expected)}, '
                    f'got {len(midi.data)} bytes'
                )
            print(f'Short messages: {len(midi.data)} bytes verified', flush=True)
            midi.data.clear()
            # Non-commercial SysEx; stream slowly enough for conventional MIDI.
            sysex = b'\xf0\x7d' + bytes(i % 128 for i in range(4096)) + b'\xf7'
            for i in range(0, len(sysex), 60):
                midi.send(destination, sysex[i : i + 60])
                time.sleep(0.025)
            time.sleep(0.2)
            expected = sysex if options.expect_enabled else b''
            if bytes(midi.data) != expected:
                raise ValueError(
                    f'SysEx mismatch: expected {len(expected)}, '
                    f'got {len(midi.data)} bytes'
                )
            print(f'Streamed SysEx: {len(midi.data)} bytes verified', flush=True)
            if options.stress_seconds:
                peers = [
                    v for k, v in destinations.items() if 'cntrl experimental' in k
                ]
                deadline = time.monotonic() + options.stress_seconds
                calls = 0
                while time.monotonic() < deadline:
                    for p in peers:
                        midi.send(p, messages)
                    calls += 1
                    time.sleep(0.001)
                time.sleep(0.5)
                print(f'Overload: {calls} bursts to {len(peers)} outputs', flush=True)
            for i in range(9):
                print(client.request(f'CNTRL MIDI STATUS {i}'), flush=True)
    finally:
        midi.close()

class Outline:
    def __init__(self, path: Path, horizontal_scale: float = 1.0) -> None:
        self.horizontal_scale = horizontal_scale
        self.data = path.read_bytes()
        self.face = freetype.Face.from_bytes(self.data)
        self.hb = uharfbuzz.Font(uharfbuzz.Face(self.data))  # ty: ignore[unresolved-attribute]  # Public C extension API.
        uharfbuzz.ot_font_set_funcs(self.hb)  # ty: ignore[unresolved-attribute]  # Public C extension API.
        self.glyphs: dict[tuple[int, int], Glyph] = {}
        self.runs: dict[tuple[int, str], Run] = {}

    def descent(self, size: int) -> int:
        """Reserve the font's declared below-baseline space, even for capitals."""
        return max(0, ceil(-self.face.descender * size / self.face.units_per_EM))

    def glyph(self, size: int, identifier: int) -> Glyph:
        key = (size, identifier)
        if key not in self.glyphs:
            self.face.set_pixel_sizes(0, size)
            self.face.set_transform(
                freetype.Matrix(round(self.horizontal_scale * 65536), 0, 0, 65536),
                freetype.Vector(0, 0),
            )
            self.face.load_glyph(
                identifier,
                freetype.FT_LOAD_RENDER  # ty: ignore[unresolved-attribute]  # Public C extension API.
                | freetype.FT_LOAD_TARGET_MONO  # ty: ignore[unresolved-attribute]  # Public C extension API.
                | freetype.FT_LOAD_NO_HINTING,  # ty: ignore[unresolved-attribute]  # Public C extension API.
            )
            slot = self.face.glyph
            bitmap = slot.bitmap
            stride = (bitmap.width + 7) // 8
            source = bytes(bitmap.buffer)
            pixels = b''.join(
                source[y * bitmap.pitch : y * bitmap.pitch + stride]
                for y in range(bitmap.rows)
            )
            self.glyphs[key] = Glyph(
                identifier=identifier,
                width=bitmap.width,
                height=bitmap.rows,
                left=slot.bitmap_left,
                top=slot.bitmap_top,
                pixels=pixels,
            )
        return self.glyphs[key]

    def shape(self, size: int, text: str) -> Run:
        key = (size, text)
        if key in self.runs:
            return self.runs[key]
        self.hb.scale = (round(size * 64 * self.horizontal_scale), size * 64)
        positions: list[list[int]] = []
        x = y = 0
        left = right = top = bottom = 0
        missing: set[str] = set()
        for start, end, level, script in text_runs(text):
            buffer = uharfbuzz.Buffer()  # ty: ignore[unresolved-attribute]  # Public C extension API.
            buffer.add_codepoints([ord(c) for c in text[start:end]])
            buffer.guess_segment_properties()
            buffer.direction = 'rtl' if level % 2 else 'ltr'
            buffer.script = script
            buffer.language = 'und'
            uharfbuzz.shape(self.hb, buffer)  # ty: ignore[unresolved-attribute]  # Public C extension API.
            info, offsets = buffer.glyph_infos, buffer.glyph_positions
            assert offsets is not None
            for item in info:
                if not item.codepoint:
                    boundaries = sorted({i.cluster for i in info} | {end - start})
                    stop = next(i for i in boundaries if i > item.cluster)
                    missing.update(
                        c
                        for c in text[start + item.cluster : start + stop]
                        if unicodedata.category(c) != 'Cf'
                    )
            for item, offset in zip(info, offsets, strict=True):
                if not item.codepoint:
                    continue
                glyph = self.glyph(size, item.codepoint)
                px, py = (
                    round((x + offset.x_offset) / 64),
                    round(-(y + offset.y_offset) / 64),
                )
                positions.append([item.codepoint, px, py])
                left = min(left, px + glyph.left)
                right = max(right, px + glyph.left + glyph.width)
                top = min(top, py - glyph.top)
                bottom = max(bottom, py - glyph.top + glyph.height)
                x += offset.x_advance
                y += offset.y_advance
        if missing:
            raise MissingGlyphs(sorted(missing, key=ord))
        right = max(right, round(x / 64))
        result = Run(
            positions=positions, left=left, width=right - left, top=top, bottom=bottom
        )
        self.runs[key] = result
        return result

def text_runs(text: str) -> list[tuple[int, int, int, str]]:
    """Itemize logical script runs, then put them in bidi visual order."""
    if not text:
        return []
    if any(unicodedata.bidirectional(c) in ('LRI', 'RLI', 'FSI', 'PDI') for c in text):
        raise ValueError(
            'explicit bidi isolation controls are not supported in display labels'
        )
    storage = algorithm.get_empty_storage()
    storage['base_level'] = algorithm.get_base_level(text)
    storage['base_dir'] = 'R' if storage['base_level'] else 'L'
    algorithm.get_embedding_levels(text, storage)
    for i, c in enumerate(storage['chars']):
        c['index'] = i
    algorithm.explicit_embed_and_overrides(storage)
    algorithm.resolve_weak_types(storage)
    algorithm.resolve_neutral_types(storage, False)
    algorithm.resolve_implicit_levels(storage, False)
    # Common characters inherit the preceding script, then the following one
    # at the start. Joining controls stay within the original logical slices.
    scripts = [unicodedata.script(c) for c in text]
    previous = 'Zyyy'
    for i, s in enumerate(scripts):
        if s not in ('Zyyy', 'Zinh', 'Zzzz'):
            previous = s
        else:
            scripts[i] = previous
    following = 'Latn'
    for i in range(len(scripts) - 1, -1, -1):
        if scripts[i] not in ('Zyyy', 'Zinh', 'Zzzz'):
            following = scripts[i]
        else:
            scripts[i] = following
    groups: list[tuple[int, int, int, str]] = []
    indices: dict[int, int] = {}
    for c in storage['chars']:
        i, level = c['index'], c['level']
        if groups and groups[-1][2:] == (level, scripts[i]):
            start, _, _, script = groups[-1]
            groups[-1] = (start, i + 1, level, script)
        else:
            groups.append((i, i + 1, level, scripts[i]))
        indices[i] = len(groups) - 1
    if not groups:
        return []
    # Include ignored shaping controls at run edges too.
    groups[0] = (0, *groups[0][1:])
    groups = [
        (g[0], groups[i + 1][0] if i + 1 < len(groups) else len(text), g[2], g[3])
        for i, g in enumerate(groups)
    ]
    algorithm.reorder_resolved_levels(storage, False)
    order = list(dict.fromkeys(indices[c['index']] for c in storage['chars']))
    return [groups[i] for i in order]

def parse_storage_info(response: str) -> StorageInfo:
    fields = response.split()
    if len(fields) != 9 or fields[:2] != ['CNTRL', 'STORAGE']:
        raise ValueError(response)
    sectors, kind, identity, fat, cluster_bytes, clusters, free = fields[2:]
    cid = bytes.fromhex(identity)
    if len(cid) != 16:
        raise ValueError('Expected a 16-byte SD identification register')
    capacity = int(sectors) * 512
    unit, count = int(cluster_bytes), int(clusters)
    available = None if free == '-' else int(free)
    if available is not None and not 0 <= available <= count:
        raise ValueError('Invalid free cluster count')
    if kind not in ('1', '2', '3') or fat not in ('16', '32', '64'):
        raise ValueError('Unsupported card or filesystem type')
    card_type = {'1': 'SD v1', '2': 'SD v2', '3': 'SDHC'}[kind]
    if kind == '3' and capacity > 32 * 1024**3:
        card_type = 'SDXC'
    return StorageInfo(
        capacity_bytes=capacity,
        card_type=card_type,
        manufacturer_id=f'0x{cid[0]:02X}',
        oem_id=cid[1:3].decode('ascii'),
        product=cid[3:8].decode('ascii'),
        revision=f'{cid[8] >> 4}.{cid[8] & 15}',
        serial_number=f'0x{int.from_bytes(cid[9:13], "big"):08X}',
        manufactured=(
            f'{2000 + ((cid[13] & 15) << 4) + (cid[14] >> 4)}-{cid[14] & 15:02d}'
        ),
        filesystem={'16': 'FAT16', '32': 'FAT32', '64': 'exFAT'}[fat],
        allocation_unit_bytes=unit,
        usable_bytes=count * unit,
        free_bytes=None if available is None else available * unit,
        used_bytes=None if available is None else (count - available) * unit,
    )

    descriptor = os.open(SERIAL_PATH, os.O_RDWR | os.O_NOCTTY | os.O_NONBLOCK)
    try:
        attributes = termios.tcgetattr(descriptor)
        attributes[4] = attributes[5] = termios.B134
        termios.tcsetattr(descriptor, termios.TCSANOW, attributes)
    finally:
        os.close(descriptor)

    print('Bootloader requested; verify HalfKay enumeration before uploading.')
